decision: Keep cap256 and default cache policy. Neither reduced grid shows consistent model-sized H2D gains. Null controls prevent attributing every short-interval difference to the intended optimization.
caveats: Only standalone native v14 copy replay; no L0 arm or full-model run. Same cached kernel/module/ISA/allocations/context/data/local size and dependencies in both arms. The grid-cap candidates change only the intended group count, not actual packet addresses or physical occupancy.

At98304bytes both grid arms have24groups. These implicit null controls sometimes show appreciable differences despite identical kernel and geometry. Dedicated controls then compare two separately recorded identical lists, and one identical list reused for both labels. No arithmetic policy changes in either null run.

Each of16cases has two overwritten phases,oppositeABBA/BAAB order,12warmups+48retainedsamples per phase. All raw samples/outliers retained. Labels select the comparison arm;they do not mean different cache policy. Exact source generation and binary/module/protocol hashes verified.

GPU raw tick intervals include identical timestamp and initial state commands. Host submit/wait spans separate. Preparation,validation,uploads/readback outside timing. GPU clocks unlocked; no significance or calibrated wall-time claim.

A no-change control can reveal noise,ordering or list-state/address effects; these measurements alone do not distinguish their cause. The earlier cache report remains immutable. Its small-copy deltas are observations,not uniquely isolated causal cache costs in light of these new controls.
